How much does starter replacement cost?

A new starter motor, installed — what it costs, and what moves the price:

$565–$796
Starter replacement, national — RepairPal average

Parts $375–$516 · labor $191–$280

Bay Area: no published metro-specific figure found — the national range is the honest reference.

What drives the price

Why quotes run $300 to $1,400

Four things move the price:

Access
Labor runs $186–$272 nationally — one hour on an easy car, up to 8 under an intake manifold. This is the entire price spread.
The part
New aftermarket: $80–$350. Remanufactured: $50–$350. Luxury and rare models: $500+ for the part alone.
Vehicle
Common sedans cluster $600–$900; luxury models $900–$1,400. Trucks with buried starters bill the most labor.
Dealer vs. independent
Same pattern as everything else: dealers charge more per labor hour and full markup on the part. Independents win on this job.
New vs. remanufactured

What the extra money buys

Remanufactured
$50–$350 part

Rebuilt and tested. Starters are simple machines — a quality reman is a reasonable bet on a daily driver.

New
$80–$350+ part

Brand-new unit, longest warranty. Pick new when the labor to reach it is brutal — you don't want to do this twice.

Bottom line: match the part to the labor. Cheap part + easy access means reman is fine. Expensive labor means buy the new one and cry once.

Questions

Common questions

How do I know it's the starter?

A single loud click when you turn the key is the classic sign. Grinding or intermittent no-starts point there too — but rule out the battery first, it's cheaper.

Can I drive with a failing starter?

Until it strands you, yes. Starters often warn you — clicking, screeching — but sometimes they just quit. Don't ignore the warnings.

How long does replacement take?

Under an hour on an accessible car; half a day when the intake manifold has to come off. Ask where yours lives before approving the quote.

Starter or alternator — which is it?

Starter means it won't crank and just clicks. Alternator means it cranks fine, then dies while driving with dimming lights. Different parts, different bills.

Every car prices differently.

The range above is a national average. Your price depends on where the starter sits and which part you pick. Take a photo of your estimate in Brightglow for a second opinion on the actual car.
